summary: Focused infrastructure review completed for source HEAD 5450fc7271332ba09892350c3af28646c0d12dc0 and the four dirty reactor deployment artifacts. Two conditional operational defects were reproduced with isolated local fixtures: overlapping backups violate writer quiescence, and a preexisting permissive shared directory leaves database credentials readable while preflight accepts it.
coverage: Read the immutable review brief, run plan, effective AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, project startup context, workflow and focused-review guidance. Input SHA-256: 6d6e0a64addfa429dbb8929cc89cb801cdf10f45861fc005052112616fe4f519.

Verified all eight plan scope hashes against inspected bytes: {"Dockerfile": "ac72e727e331af0cff014d4681c78aba382d84a0e8b6d47947df495ace6d9c9f", "apps/server/src/auth/config.ts": "209c74005e490d18393ecd71f51ac84914f8b345ebcfb7a5615f9eacf70da2f7", "apps/server/src/blobs/index.ts": "f21034309a3d42c75976c9bd5ca1baa526cfa42eff40b71c7cc5aa0ba924f1d5", "apps/server/src/context.ts": "175b33033c0b5e8d043daf3e88d829c5e9aa8f1b190d1f4dc59a3e318a0bf757", "deploy/reactor/backup.py": "4f797099198c08c76b4a7641a7a5afe96e7d667f760581eefc00d0b5d1f7be57", "deploy/reactor/compose.yaml": "af7bcf79c05edef725f529268fab7350a4ba5687ecd9d7f96170867310448a6c", "deploy/reactor/initialize.py": "2763c6a6ebb315cdd1cb9078674e81d0e74bb147ad821240accf81ec260bbb62", "deploy/reactor/preflight.py": "c3e2439696aa4c1c0b00f0fa5fa8b8bdbc1eb8d1d365ebd74d5d07057346637b"}

Inspected compose service isolation, loopback port mapping, private database network, PostgreSQL initialization/secret bind paths, app non-root/read-only runtime, named volumes, restart policy, healthchecks, graceful-stop budgets and bounded logs/resources.

Traced initialized configuration against auth/config.ts, startup.ts, auth/service.ts bootstrap, context.ts database selection, blobs/index.ts and blobs/local.ts, server.ts graceful shutdown and index.ts signal handlers. The staged settings use production OIDC, disable seed/repository scans, select PostgreSQL/local evidence and do not provision an owner or identity provider.

Traced backup.py stop/dump/globals/artifact/config/hash/finally-restart flow against Dockerfile CMD, runtime blob permissions and shutdown behavior. The tar entrypoint overrides the application CMD, so the artifact helper does not intentionally start an application writer.

Executed one isolated Python fixture harness in /Users/artem/visua with subprocess.run mocked for all Docker commands. Forced two backup invocations to pass their running checks together, delayed B during its database dump, and allowed A to finish/restart. Both scripts completed; artifact observations were A: app stopped, B: app running.

Executed initialize.py and preflight.py against an isolated tempfile install with a preexisting shared directory set to 0755 and dummy generated secrets; inspected only permissions and readiness booleans. Observed shared=0755, app.env=0600, init.sql=0444, postgres-admin-password=0444, preflight exit=0 and private_install_ready=true.
Parsed initialize.py, preflight.py and backup.py with ast.parse successfully. No real Docker, SSH, container, account, credential, service, shared build/test or Git mutation was performed.

findings.mechanism: Two scheduled/manual backups can both observe a running app before either stops it. There is no per-install lock. One invocation can complete first and execute its finally restart while the other is still dumping SQL or capturing evidence. The latter then reports a complete backup whose database and artifacts need not describe one quiescent state; its manifest assertion that the app stayed stopped throughout is false.
findings.evidence: Source checks writer state independently at line 30, stops at line 34, captures at lines 37-45 and always restarts at line 64. A deterministic two-thread fixture executing the unmodified source with mocked subprocess.run returned complete for A and B, while B observed app_running_during_artifact_capture=true after A restarted. This reproduces script coordination only, not a real database corruption or restore failure.
findings.recommendation: Acquire an exclusive per-install lock before the initial state check and retain it through backup finalization and restart. Reject or wait on overlapping invocations; preserve the existing restart-on-command-failure behavior and recheck the overlapping schedule.

findings.mechanism: If the operator has already created shared with normal 0755 permissions under traversable installation ancestors, mkdir(exist_ok=True) keeps that mode. The initializer then changes init.sql and postgres-admin-password to 0444, exposing both database-role passwords to other host accounts. Its comment assumes the parent is 0700, but does not enforce it, and preflight checks only app.env permissions and accepts this state.
findings.evidence: In an isolated fixture with a preexisting 0755 shared directory, the unmodified initializer left shared=0755 and produced init.sql=0444 and postgres-admin-password=0444. The unmodified preflight exited 0 with private_install_ready=true. The fixture establishes modes and acceptance; actual cross-account reachability additionally depends on installation ancestor permissions and was not tested.
findings.recommendation: Before creating secrets, reject symlink/untrusted shared directories and enforce private ownership and 0700 permissions, or fail clearly if unable. Have preflight validate the enclosing credential directory and relevant credential paths; retain the container-readable file modes only behind the verified private host directory.

limitations: Fresh bounded native-subagent context was supplied by the lead. This is one focused infrastructure/script pass, not an application-security assessment or approval for live-user admission.

No remote or live runtime inspection was authorized. Actual reactor directory ownership/modes, Docker/Compose version, deployed image identities, PostgreSQL entrypoint execution, volume ownership, network behavior, restart success and host workload isolation were not measured.

Docker subprocesses in the concurrency check returned fixture data. No real SQL or tar archive was produced, no actual corruption was demonstrated and no restore or application-integrity acceptance was performed.

The confidentiality issue is conditional on traversable installation ancestors and a preexisting permissive shared directory. A newly created shared directory is 0700; an independently protected ancestor also limits exposure.

Backup archive hashes establish captured-byte checksums only. Consistency relies on a sole writer plus uninterrupted quiescence; independent off-host/encrypted retention, fresh-volume restoration, roles/ownership, database/entity/audit checks and reviewed artifact-byte recovery remain separate acceptance work.

Package/base-image advisories and previously reported application findings were outside the bounded assignment and remain unresolved. No provider login, owner bootstrap, public HTTPS routing, capacity or release-readiness conclusion is established.
